notes:
Summary: Labyrinth is a marketplace vertical (fashion resale) with a heavy returns/refund workload — primary automation thesis is to reduce agent handle time and automate refund/tool calls while keeping strict PCI and data residency controls. They run a proprietary ticketing backend (ThreadCore) with an API that accepts create/update operations and webhooks for status. Key ask: enable safe tool-calling from agent-assist flows to create/update tickets, trigger refunds via payment gateway, and escalate to a SafetyOps team via Slack/webhook when rules match.

Recent activity / timeline:
- 2025-11-05: Intro call (AE: Avery) — business goals + cost sensitivity. Interested in 50-150k ARR purchase.
- 2025-11-18: Solution demo (SE: Ravi) — walkthrough of agent-assist + tool-calling to ThreadCore; asked about function-calling safety.
- 2026-01-12: Security deep-dive (ff_2026-01-12_7843) — legal asks about PCI and retention; provided Security FAQ (drive link).
- 2026-02-05: Technical POC kickoff (ff_2026-02-05_9122) — stubbed integration to ThreadCore sandbox, initial token limits applied.
- 2026-02-20: Pre-POC infra call — agreed to 72-hour load window for spike testing, Redwood to provide dedicated instance suggestion and batching profile.

Technical requirements / acceptance criteria (customer language):
- Tool-calling: must be atomic and idempotent for ticket create/update; guarantees for at-least-once vs exactly-once documented.
- Latency: agent-facing tool-calls should be sub-250ms median; overall agent assist turn should be <600ms on average.
- Throughput: baseline 150 req/s for autosuggest + tool-calls; expected holiday spikes up to 450 req/s sustained for 30–60 minutes.
- Reliability: automatic fallback to smaller model variant or cached KB answer during capacity constraints; audit trail for each tool-call (who/which model/request id).
- Safety: redact payment tokens before logs; KMS-backed encryption for secrets; SSO/SAML for console access.

Model & routing preferences:
- Prefer open weights where possible (quantized Llama2-style) to reduce egress cost; allow hosted LLM for early POC to speed up eval.
- Need structured function-calling support (tool schemas) to map agent intent -> ThreadCore API payload.
- Routing policy: primary to dedicated pool (for latency guarantees), fallback to hosted smaller model in different region if capacity constrained.

POC plan and success metrics:
- Phase 1 (sandbox): wire ThreadCore sandbox -> Redwood dev instance; validate create/update ticket flows and webhook handling. Measure p99 latency and error rate.
- Phase 2 (load): execute 72-hour spike test (expected peak 450 req/s). Redwood to supply batching config and autoscale recommendations. Success = <1% tool-call error, p95 <500ms.
- Phase 3 (security & SLA): SSO + KMS integration, final legal signoff on PCI scope.

Quotes / verbatims:
- "We need refunds to be safe and auditable — cannot have duplicate refunds from retries." — Head of Ops
- "If you can show reliable handling during holiday spikes we can move forward quickly." — CTO

Integration notes / open technical questions:
- ThreadCore auth: OAuth2 client credentials supported; need example JWT flow for private deployment.
- Refund flow touches payment gateway X — legal wants to confirm whether Redwood will see masked payment tokens or if a proxy pattern is required.
- Can Redwood provide per-request routing headers for downstream observability? SE asked for trace-id passthrough.

Next steps (short):
- SE (Ravi) to provision POC config and threading rules by 2026-03-03.
- Infra sync w/ Labyrinth on VPC peering window (dates tentatively 2026-03-10).
- Legal to confirm PCI scoping; aim for signoff during 72-hour POC.
